steps.instructions: Phase 1/3 RECON (test strategist): read the code and the requirements in scope (the operator's ask, any linked requirements or issue) and the repository's existing tests; detect the test harness (vitest/jest/pytest/Playwright/node:test). Map the behaviours to test, the risks by likelihood and impact, and which behaviours existing tests already cover — cite file:line for anything you claim is covered. GROUND FIRST: query the code graph through the wicked-garden-search skill and the read-only estate shim, one call per lookup: "$WICKED_GARDEN_ROOT/scripts/wicked-garden" run scripts/_estate_client.py --readonly call '{"tool":"SearchEntity","arguments":{"name":"<symbol>"}}' (always --readonly); then open and read every file you cite, at the lines you cite. Read with git and your file and search tools directly; do not run `python -c` or other inline-interpreter probes (the read-only boundary refuses them). Analysis only: write no files.

Phase 2/3 PLAN (test strategist): write ONE file, docs/test-plans/<slug>.md (kebab-case slug of the subject). It holds: scope and what is out of scope; the behaviours under test; scenarios grouped by behaviour, each with a positive and a negative case, its priority from the risk ranking, the level (unit, integration, end-to-end) and the harness and command it would run under; the existing tests it relies on (file:line); test data and environment needs; and the open questions. Write no test code and touch no other file. Never push, never open or edit a pull request — the run's deliver phase does that.

Phase 3/3 CHECK (independent evaluator): List EVERY change the run made, not only the committed diff: committed (git diff --name-status against the run's base), staged and unstaged (git diff --name-status HEAD; git diff --cached --name-status) and untracked (git ls-files --others --exclude-standard), including deletions and renames. The only allowed output is ONE new or updated Markdown file docs/test-plans/<kebab-case-slug>.md; FAIL on any other change (source, tests, config, other docs, deletions, renames). Then read the plan file and judge it: every claim of existing coverage verified at file:line, the high-risk behaviours not missed, every scenario has its negative case, priorities follow the risk, and each scenario names a harness the repository really has. List the gaps, most important first. PASS only when only that file changed and every claim of existing coverage holds at file:line, every scenario has its negative case and names a harness the repository has, and no high-risk behaviour is missing; anything else is a FAIL. End with one plain-text line VERDICT: PASS or VERDICT: FAIL as the last line, findings above it; never quote another VERDICT line. Read-only: change nothing.
